cells.tense: The compass is steady, and it can be read while you stand among others.
cells.ask: Take a custom your group still keeps and work out, on paper or in your head, what it grew in you about fair. Gather that one lesson and keep it where you can find it again.
cells.core:
Your sense of what's fair is working, and it works best among people who share something. You can feel which parts of what the group hands down are still true, and you can feel what's owed between people, and the two readings agree. Nothing is being argued in you. That is why others come to you when something has been decided wrong.

A custom you carry has already proved itself worth keeping. Gather what it grew and set the lesson down where the custom lives, because meaning stays alive while somebody keeps it. A practice that runs on and never gets tended slowly stops belonging to anyone.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's fair, and it holds among people.
cells.verb: weighing what is fair against what is owed, by feel
cells.place: in the shared meaning a group carries — its rituals, its sayings, what it keeps alive

cells.tense: You are already braced for the argument that follows a thing you have not said yet.
cells.act: hold someone else up with what you have
cells.ask: When something lands wrong in your group, hold back the corrected version. Notice what you saw, keep it to yourself, and let the room carry on without your tally.
cells.core:
The weighing has run past the moment it belongs to. Among people you share ground with, you're deciding how it will land on you before anyone has moved. The compass makes its rounds twice and argues with itself in between. You arrive with the verdict already formed.

Some of that strength can go where it's actually needed. When someone gets something wrong, they don't need your tally. They need one clear observation and the room to use it. Fairness settles when you stop bracing long enough to let it. Give and take gets easier once your hand is open on the table.

cells.tense: The reading was there, and the moment it belonged to is already behind you.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: Point the way on paper: leave a short note of something you know about your group's ways where a newcomer will find it. Put it down and go.
cells.core:
You've stopped bringing the reading into the room. Among people who share something, the compass is quiet now — the sense of what's owed comes late, after the thing was decided, when nothing is left to weigh. The part of you that could say something plain stepped back and hasn't stepped forward since.

What was learned is still real, and it can move again before it moves inward. Direction doesn't need you to want to say it; it needs a route. Put down one honest piece of what you found, for someone who will need it, and walk away from it. The reading starts working the moment it leaves your hands.

cells.tense: You are doing the fairness work in the room and calling it nothing much.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Sort one conviction you hold about how your group should do things: whose voice is it in? Keep the part that's yours; hand the rest back.
cells.core:
The compass is the one doing the pointing, and your account of it leaves that out. You'll say the group decided, or that's just how it's done here, while your sense of what was owed did the deciding. It steers the room and then gets filed as custom.

What you carry is really yours, so test whether it holds. Trace the pull running through your reasons back to where it started, and the line separates into what someone taught you and what you felt and kept. Most of it will survive that look. What's left standing is a read you can trust without borrowed cover, and you can say it in your own voice next time it matters.
